label: churn100-s2
summary: This churn model (training AUC 0.901) has two main churn routes. Heavy daytime use raises risk through the direct edges (total day minutes 2.02 per sd, the largest edge; switching all direct edges off lowers training AUC to 0.539). Low daytime use combined with many customer service calls raises risk through the usage hinge, which switches off at higher day minutes the more calls a customer has made and is stronger when the evening charge is low (switching it off lowers AUC to 0.763). With four calls, an otherwise typical Georgia customer's risk is U-shaped in day minutes: 83% at very low use, 17% at moderate use and 96% at very high use. A separate gate adds risk from four calls upward outside West Virginia (it acts on 306 training customers; the West Virginia exception rests on the 12 customers in that state with four or more calls). A voice mail plan lowers risk through its direct edge (-0.99 per sd) and an always-on chain, and international plan (0.75 per sd) raises it. State terms shift the score for several states; Nevada's downward shift is fitted to 77 customers and is not supported by their churn rate (18% against a mean predicted risk of 12%). One unit of the small state gate (node 252) is described, not explained: its output weight is tiny.
